pathway.title: RXO, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Revenue is large, rate-driven and short-dated, so its growth says little about debt capacity. Revenue rose 18.7% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, but the issuer attributes the third-quarter rise of 31.7% to revenue per load up 48% against 2% more loads, and the only firm obligations it counts beyond a year, fixed-consideration contracts of USD 51 million, are 0.78% of last-twelve-month revenue of USD 6,539 million. Because freight rates and fuel pass through to revenue, debt service rests on gross profit, which rose only 2.77% in the nine months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 9, 21, 23; calculation C07; calculation C12; calculation C13

- Margin, not volume or scale, is the pressure point and it has eroded for three years in both soft and tight freight markets. Cost of transportation rose from 75.6% of revenue in 2023 to 82.5% in the nine months of 2026; the issuer ties the 2025 and 2026 rises to capacity leaving the market after regulatory changes, which pushed carrier buy rates up faster than contract sell rates, and the 2024 report shows the same squeeze when lower freight rates were not fully offset by cheaper purchased transportation. Gross profit margin fell from 24.45% to 17.53% and adjusted EBITDA margin from 3.41% to 1.77%. Last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 116 million is below the USD 134 million of 2023 on revenue 66.51% higher, so growth has not added earnings. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C11

- Recent earnings improvement came from spreading overhead over a larger, rate-inflated revenue base, not from wider margins, and the same operating leverage works in reverse. Overhead (direct operating expense plus selling, general and administrative expense) rose only 2.19% in the nine months of 2026 while revenue rose 18.7%, taking it from 21.03% of revenue in 2023 to 15.62% and lifting third-quarter adjusted EBITDA to USD 51 million from USD 30 million; it still absorbs 89.96% of gross profit, so each 1 pp of revenue lost to carrier cost removes USD 65.39 million, or 56.37% of adjusted EBITDA. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 49, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 21–22; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C21

- Leverage is moderate only on the issuer-adjusted measure, and that measure is the weak point. Net debt of USD 471 million is 4.06x adjusted but 8.41x reported EBITDA, up from 2.75x adjusted at the end of 2024, and the USD 60 million of add-backs are 51.72% of adjusted EBITDA; restructuring recurs in every period and the issuer paid USD 25 million of restructuring cash in the nine months, so the add-backs are not all non-cash or one-off. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8–9; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03

- Free cash flow is negative in every period shown and borrowing funds the gap. It was negative USD 57 million in 2024, negative USD 8 million in 2025 and negative USD 73 million over the last twelve months; before working capital, adjusted EBITDA less cash interest, cash taxes and capital spending leaves only USD 22 million, which is less than the USD 25 million of restructuring cash paid in nine months. Total debt rose USD 92 million since the end of 2025 to fund receivables growth of USD 252 million, partly offset by payables growth of USD 169 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4, 9, 25; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C16

- Liquidity and distant maturities are the main support, but their strength cannot be tested. Cash of USD 25 million and USD 335 million of secured-facility availability give USD 360 million, nothing of size matures before 2031, and the unsecured notes sold in February 2026 were valued at 97.50% of principal at 2026-09-30; yet the facility's fixed charge coverage, minimum liquidity and minimum excess availability tests have no stated levels, so how far earnings can fall before borrowing is restricted is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04; calculation C17; calculation C18

- Customer spread is a real support, while the asset base behind unsecured creditors is thin. The largest customer was 11.4% of 2025 revenue, the top five 23% and the top 20 37%, and retail and e-commerce, the largest vertical, 37.4%; against that, equity of USD 1,516 million is less than goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,533 million, so tangible equity is negative USD 17 million and the unsecured noteholders rank behind a first-priority secured facility with commitments of USD 450 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14; calculation C19

- The pending sale to C.H. Robinson dominates event risk, and its direction for creditors is not established. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027; RXO may owe a termination fee of USD 175 million, equal to 48.61% of liquidity, needs the buyer's consent for actions outside the ordinary course and has a holder of about 19% committed to vote for the deal, but no filing states what happens to the notes or the secured facility. Past financial policy was conservative, with no dividends, an unused repurchase authorization of USD 123 million and an equity-funded 2024 acquisition, which favours standalone creditors. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 29–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 53; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14; calculation C20

cells.text: Brokered transportation platform with an asset-light model: RXO places shippers' freight with independent carriers using its technology and prices on a contract or spot basis; largest component is truck brokerage, with managed transportation and last mile alongside.
Cash flow depends on the spread between what shippers pay and what carriers are paid, so it is a margin business with little fixed capital.
Truck brokerage 73.6% of 2025 revenue, last mile 20.8%, managed transportation 9.6% and eliminations -4.0%; one reportable segment.
Truck brokerage dominates and is the most cyclical line; the other two use the same digital platform and add cross-selling.
Largest customer 11.4% of 2025 revenue (USD 653 million), top five about 23% and top 20 about 37%; end markets led by retail and e-commerce.
Moderate concentration: a single loss would hurt but not break the revenue base.
Non-exclusive one-year renewable agreements with independent carriers who are solely responsible for their service.
Capacity is rented, not owned, so cost follows market buy rates and tight capacity squeezes margin before it hurts volume.
Cost of transportation was 82.2% of third-quarter 2026 revenue against 80.0% a year earlier; selling, general and administrative expense fell to 11.9% of revenue from 14.6%.
Higher purchased-transportation cost took most of the operating-leverage gain from lower overhead.
Receivables rose with higher freight prices and revenue; payables rose by less; the issuer says debt funded the working-capital need.
Rising freight prices consume cash before they raise profit, which is why debt rose while earnings were thin.
Self-insurance programs, partly through a captive insurer, plus purchased cover; misclassification claims are generally outside insurance.
Claims experience flows through cash and earnings and is audited as a critical estimate.
Brokers are licensed by the federal motor carrier regulator and face negligent-selection suits; classification of independent contractors is contested by regulators and litigants.
Legal change could add cost or liability without any change in volume.
9,218 team members at 2025 year end, of whom fewer than 20 were under collective agreements.
Variable-compensation costs move with profit, giving some cost flexibility.

runs.text: The ranked strengths are, first, liquidity of USD 360 million with nothing of size due before 2031, which at the current cash burn would last several years if availability holds; second, an asset-light model whose capital spending is 0.89% of revenue and is discretionary by the issuer's account, which gives management a cash lever; third, moderate customer concentration with a largest customer of 11.4% of revenue, which limits the damage from one loss; fourth, overhead that rose only 2.19% in nine months while revenue rose 18.7%, which shows the cost base can be held when revenue grows; and fifth, demonstrated access to the unsecured bond market in February 2026, with the notes valued at 97.50% of principal at 2026-09-30. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 49, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10–12, 24; calculation C04; calculation C09; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C18

The ranked weaknesses are, first, carrier buy rates that have risen faster than contract sell rates, taking cost of transportation from 75.6% to 82.5% of revenue and adjusted EBITDA margin to 1.77%; second, negative free cash flow of USD 73 million over the last twelve months that is funded by debt; third, reliance on add-backs that are 51.72% of adjusted EBITDA; fourth, overhead that absorbs 89.96% of gross profit, so small falls in gross profit cut earnings sharply; and fifth, event and documentation risk, because the sale terms for the debt and the covenant levels are not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 10–11, 16, 21; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C08; calculation C10

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: C.H. Robinson Worldwide, Inc. agreed on 2026-10-04 to acquire RXO in a two-step merger that leaves RXO as a wholly owned subsidiary, for USD 17.25 in cash plus 0.0856 C.H. Robinson shares per RXO share, an implied USD 30.25 per share and about USD 5.8 billion in total. Holders may elect cash, shares or the mix, subject to proration, and closing needs approval by holders of a majority of RXO shares, regulatory approvals and customary conditions; the expected close is the first half of 2027. RXO would owe a termination fee of USD 175 million in specified circumstances, may not solicit competing offers beyond limited exceptions, needs C.H. Robinson's consent for actions outside the ordinary course, and has a holder of about 19% committed to vote in favour. The announced USD 5.8 billion is not defined in the filing: the per-share price on the basic share count gives about USD 4,990 million and on diluted weighted shares about USD 5,203 million, so the headline probably includes debt, but that is not stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18–19, 29–32; calculation C03; calculation C04

RXO changed its debt in 2026 before the merger was agreed. On 2026-02-05 it replaced its unsecured revolving credit facility with a USD 450 million asset-based facility secured by a first priority interest in all assets of the credit parties other than real property, and on 2026-02-20 it sold USD 400 million of unsecured notes due 2031 and redeemed all of its notes due 2027 at 101.875% of principal. In the second quarter it added a small non-U.S. revolving credit facility. For creditors the secured facility ranks ahead of the unsecured notes over those assets, while the maturity wall moved from 2027 to 2031. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 11; Source readiness (CP-0)

The filings state nothing on how the merger affects either instrument: there is no change-of-control term for the notes, no statement of whether C.H. Robinson will refinance, assume or guarantee the debt, and no financing commitment for the cash portion of the price. These terms sit in the merger agreement and the note indenture, which were not supplied, so the effect of the transaction on creditors is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 16, 32; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.value: The five supplied RXO filings support a credit snapshot of the consolidated company through 2026-09-30, but not covenant, ratings or market-based work, so any view of creditor protection while the C.H. Robinson takeover is pending remains provisional.

fields.value: Both annual reports and the three 2026 quarterly reports give statements, debt notes and liquidity disclosure that agree where they overlap, and the quarters add up to the nine-month totals, apart from two small differences logged under Gaps. The takeover agreement signed on 2026-10-04 is known only from a summary in the latest quarterly report. fields.value: - Material: The ABL credit agreement, the indenture for the 2031 notes and the earlier revolving credit agreement were not supplied; the annual report and the first quarterly report of 2026 list them as exhibits only. The ABL Facility's three financial covenants (fixed charge coverage ratio, minimum liquidity and minimum excess availability) are named without levels, test dates or definitions, and the borrowing base inputs behind the USD 335 million of availability are not printed. Covenant headroom is not calculable and availability can only be taken as stated. The only covenant levels printed are those of the earlier unsecured revolver (interest coverage of at least 3.00 to 1.00 and consolidated leverage of at most 4.50 to 1.00), which was terminated on 2026-02-05.

The latest quarterly report gives the consideration, the election and proration mechanics, the closing conditions, an expected close in the first half of 2027, a USD 175 million termination fee and holder voting support. It does not say how RXO's notes and ABL Facility are treated on a change of control, whether C.H. Robinson will assume, refinance or repay them, or what limits apply to RXO's borrowing before closing. A search of all five filings found no change-of-control debt term; the only change-of-control text is a Delaware takeover statute described in the annual reports.

Business & governance can describe management and the largest named holder but cannot assess board independence or alignment.

fields.value: The strongest counterweight is that the cash outflow is working capital, not operating losses: receivables rose USD 252 million since the end of 2025 while payables rose USD 169 million as higher freight prices lifted revenue, and that investment should reverse if rates ease. fields.value: Carrying debt rose from USD 368 million at 2024-12-31 to USD 404 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 496 million at 2026-09-30, while cash stayed between USD 17 million and USD 35 million, so net debt climbed from USD 333 million to USD 471 million. The USD 92 million increase in debt since the end of 2025 is, in the issuer's words, borrowing to fund working capital as revenue grew. Reported EBITDA, which is operating income plus depreciation and amortization and so carries restructuring, integration and impairment charges, was USD 56 million over the last twelve months and gives net leverage of 8.41x; on the issuer-adjusted measure of USD 116 million the same net debt is 4.06x. The distance between the two answers is the main credit judgement in this module: the adjusted measure rests on add-backs whose recurrence is untested, and restructuring costs appear in every period shown.

fields.value: Operating cash flow was negative USD 22 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 against positive USD 44 million a year earlier, and negative USD 15 million over the last twelve months. Receivables absorbed USD 261 million of cash in the nine months, partly offset by a USD 175 million rise in payables, as higher freight rates and fuel prices lifted revenue per load. Capital spending of USD 42 million leaves free cash flow of negative USD 64 million for the nine months and negative USD 73 million over the last twelve months, financed by borrowing. This is a working-capital float rather than an operating loss: payables fund much of the receivables, so a fall in freight prices would release cash from receivables but also shrink payables, and the net effect is not established. The issuer describes truck brokerage as generating robust free cash flow conversion; that is not visible in these figures.

fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction facts for RXO, Inc. (issuer rxo-1929561), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: what the company does, who controls it, how it is governed and funded, and the pending sale to C.H. Robinson, from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness answer.

fields.value: No source outside the five filings was used, and no earlier module other than Source readiness was supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: RXO is an asset-light freight broker with moderate customer concentration and no dividend history, but its pending sale to competitor C.H. Robinson makes control, not operations, the main creditor question, and the filings do not say how the debt is treated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business earns a spread between what shippers pay and what carriers are paid, so the pressure point is margin: in the third quarter of 2026 the cost of transportation rose to 82.2% of revenue from 80.0% as buy rates outran contract sell rates. The largest customer was 11.4% of 2025 revenue and the top five 23%, so concentration is moderate. Governance evidence is thin because board independence, ownership and related-party detail sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating risk sits in the spread between buy rates and sell rates, not in assets. Truck brokerage was 73.6% of 2025 revenue and 76.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue, its purchased transportation is a variable cost, and when capacity tightened the cost of transportation climbed to 82.2% of third-quarter revenue from 80.0%; margin, not volume, is what protects debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is moderate and end markets are spread. The largest customer was 11.4% of 2025 revenue, the top five 23% and the top 20 37%, and retail and e-commerce, the largest vertical, was 37.4%, so losing one customer would not remove most of the revenue base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance looks conventional but is under-evidenced. RXO has never paid a cash dividend, funded the 2024 Coyote acquisition with new equity rather than debt, and reports effective internal controls with a clean audit opinion; against that, the chair and chief executive roles are combined in the 2025 report where the 2024 report named a non-executive chairman, and the filings do not explain the change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pending sale is the dominant event risk. C.H. Robinson would acquire RXO for cash and shares at an implied USD 5.8 billion, expected to close in the first half of 2027; a holder of about 19% has agreed to vote in favour, RXO owes a USD 175 million termination fee in specified cases, and its freedom to act outside the ordinary course is restricted until closing. Nothing supplied says how the notes or the ABL Facility are treated on closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contingent liabilities sit in last mile. Claims that delivery contractors should be treated as employees are unquantified, largely outside insurance and indemnified to the former parent; settlements to date are accrued and immaterial, so the exposure is a tail risk rather than a current charge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The acquirer is itself a named primary competitor, so regulatory clearance is part of closing risk, and RXO's customers and carriers may react during the wait.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is that part of the price is paid in cash and that RXO's own record is conservative: an equity-funded acquisition, no dividends, no distressed exchange or covenant waiver described, and a 2026 refinancing that moved maturities to 2031. If the merger agreement shows the notes and the ABL Facility left outstanding with the acquirer's support, or repaid at par or above (no filing states the acquirer's credit standing), the event risk would turn into a credit positive. If it shows RXO bearing acquisition debt, tighter restrictions or a regulatory remedy that sells business lines, the view would worsen. A further rise in the cost of transportation from sustained buy-rate pressure would weaken the view whatever happens to the merger.

fields.value: C.H. Robinson Worldwide, Inc. agreed on 2026-10-04 to acquire RXO in a two-step merger that leaves RXO as a wholly owned subsidiary, for USD 17.25 in cash plus 0.0856 C.H. Robinson shares per RXO share, an implied USD 30.25 per share and about USD 5.8 billion in total. Holders may elect cash, shares or the mix, subject to proration, and closing needs approval by holders of a majority of RXO shares, regulatory approvals and customary conditions; the expected close is the first half of 2027. RXO would owe a termination fee of USD 175 million in specified circumstances, may not solicit competing offers beyond limited exceptions, needs C.H. Robinson's consent for actions outside the ordinary course, and has a holder of about 19% committed to vote in favour. The announced USD 5.8 billion is not defined in the filing: the per-share price on the basic share count gives about USD 4,990 million and on diluted weighted shares about USD 5,203 million, so the headline probably includes debt, but that is not stated.

These terms sit in the merger agreement and the note indenture, which were not supplied, so the effect of the transaction on creditors is not established.

Scope: the consolidated company's business, margin, cash conversion, liquidity, refinancing capacity and event risk, from the five supplied filings and the three earlier answers (Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No source outside the five filings was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: RXO is an adequate business with a weak financial profile: debt of USD 496 million is 4.28x adjusted but 8.86x reported EBITDA and free cash flow is negative, so USD 360 million of liquidity and a 2031 maturity wall, not earnings, protect creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9–11; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending sale to C.H. Robinson is the swing factor, because the filings do not say whether the notes and the secured facility are repaid, assumed or left outstanding; this view is standalone and would change with the merger terms. Earnings are improving, with third-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 51 million against USD 30 million a year earlier, but through operating leverage on rate-inflated revenue rather than wider margins.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue is large, rate-driven and short-dated, so its growth says little about debt capacity. Revenue rose 18.7% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, but the issuer attributes the third-quarter rise of 31.7% to revenue per load up 48% against 2% more loads, and the only firm obligations it counts beyond a year, fixed-consideration contracts of USD 51 million, are 0.78% of last-twelve-month revenue of USD 6,539 million. Because freight rates and fuel pass through to revenue, debt service rests on gross profit, which rose only 2.77% in the nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 9, 21, 23; calculation C07; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin, not volume or scale, is the pressure point and it has eroded for three years in both soft and tight freight markets. Cost of transportation rose from 75.6% of revenue in 2023 to 82.5% in the nine months of 2026; the issuer ties the 2025 and 2026 rises to capacity leaving the market after regulatory changes, which pushed carrier buy rates up faster than contract sell rates, and the 2024 report shows the same squeeze when lower freight rates were not fully offset by cheaper purchased transportation. Gross profit margin fell from 24.45% to 17.53% and adjusted EBITDA margin from 3.41% to 1.77%. Last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 116 million is below the USD 134 million of 2023 on revenue 66.51% higher, so growth has not added earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Recent earnings improvement came from spreading overhead over a larger, rate-inflated revenue base, not from wider margins, and the same operating leverage works in reverse. Overhead (direct operating expense plus selling, general and administrative expense) rose only 2.19% in the nine months of 2026 while revenue rose 18.7%, taking it from 21.03% of revenue in 2023 to 15.62% and lifting third-quarter adjusted EBITDA to USD 51 million from USD 30 million; it still absorbs 89.96% of gross profit, so each 1 pp of revenue lost to carrier cost removes USD 65.39 million, or 56.37% of adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 49, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 21–22; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is moderate only on the issuer-adjusted measure, and that measure is the weak point. Net debt of USD 471 million is 4.06x adjusted but 8.41x reported EBITDA, up from 2.75x adjusted at the end of 2024, and the USD 60 million of add-backs are 51.72% of adjusted EBITDA; restructuring recurs in every period and the issuer paid USD 25 million of restructuring cash in the nine months, so the add-backs are not all non-cash or one-off.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8–9; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow is negative in every period shown and borrowing funds the gap. It was negative USD 57 million in 2024, negative USD 8 million in 2025 and negative USD 73 million over the last twelve months; before working capital, adjusted EBITDA less cash interest, cash taxes and capital spending leaves only USD 22 million, which is less than the USD 25 million of restructuring cash paid in nine months. Total debt rose USD 92 million since the end of 2025 to fund receivables growth of USD 252 million, partly offset by payables growth of USD 169 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4, 9, 25; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and distant maturities are the main support, but their strength cannot be tested. Cash of USD 25 million and USD 335 million of secured-facility availability give USD 360 million, nothing of size matures before 2031, and the unsecured notes sold in February 2026 were valued at 97.50% of principal at 2026-09-30; yet the facility's fixed charge coverage, minimum liquidity and minimum excess availability tests have no stated levels, so how far earnings can fall before borrowing is restricted is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04; calculation C17; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer spread is a real support, while the asset base behind unsecured creditors is thin. The largest customer was 11.4% of 2025 revenue, the top five 23% and the top 20 37%, and retail and e-commerce, the largest vertical, 37.4%; against that, equity of USD 1,516 million is less than goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,533 million, so tangible equity is negative USD 17 million and the unsecured noteholders rank behind a first-priority secured facility with commitments of USD 450 million.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pending sale to C.H. Robinson dominates event risk, and its direction for creditors is not established. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027; RXO may owe a termination fee of USD 175 million, equal to 48.61% of liquidity, needs the buyer's consent for actions outside the ordinary course and has a holder of about 19% committed to vote for the deal, but no filing states what happens to the notes or the secured facility. Past financial policy was conservative, with no dividends, an unused repurchase authorization of USD 123 million and an equity-funded 2024 acquisition, which favours standalone creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 29–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 53; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak view is the third-quarter turn and the nature of the cash outflow. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 51 million against USD 30 million a year earlier and reported EBITDA USD 45 million against USD 19 million, with gross profit up 17.25%; the cash drain is mostly working capital tied to freight rates, which may release if rates ease although payables would shrink too and the net effect is not established, capital spending is discretionary by the issuer's own account at 0.89% of revenue, interest is covered 4.00x on the adjusted measure, and the next maturity of size is 2031. A sale to a larger strategic buyer could also remove standalone risk if the debt is repaid at par or above or supported by the acquirer, although no filing states its credit standing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 24, 27; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C12; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the merger agreement and the note indenture show the notes repaid or assumed, if the credit agreement shows wide covenant headroom and borrowing-base room, or if cost of transportation falls below 82.5% of revenue for two quarters while free cash flow after working capital turns positive. It would worsen if cost of transportation reaches 83.5% of revenue with gross profit falling, if a termination fee is paid in cash, or if availability falls well below USD 335 million.

fields.value: - The credit agreement and the note indenture were not supplied, so the conclusion that liquidity protects creditors rests on stated availability and a compliance statement; it cannot show how far earnings could fall before the fixed charge coverage, minimum liquidity or minimum excess availability tests restrict borrowing.

fields.value: - The issuer states no consolidated adjusted EBITDA, so every leverage and cover conclusion on the adjusted measure uses a calculated figure that no covenant or earnings release confirms; if the add-backs were disallowed, net leverage would move toward the 8.41x on reported EBITDA.

fields.value: - The filings give no split between contract and spot revenue, no margin per load and no repricing dates, so the margin conclusion cannot say how quickly sell rates would catch up with buy rates if capacity returns, or how fast they would fall in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings carry no guidance, forecast, rating or peer data, and one fair value is the only market datapoint, so the outlook and downside conclusions are analyst judgement built on reported trends and the comparison with typical leveraged issuers is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No acquirer financing, guarantee or change-of-control term for the debt is stated, so the conclusion that the sale is the swing factor cannot be turned into a direction: it may help or hurt noteholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ranked strengths are, first, liquidity of USD 360 million with nothing of size due before 2031, which at the current cash burn would last several years if availability holds; second, an asset-light model whose capital spending is 0.89% of revenue and is discretionary by the issuer's account, which gives management a cash lever; third, moderate customer concentration with a largest customer of 11.4% of revenue, which limits the damage from one loss; fourth, overhead that rose only 2.19% in nine months while revenue rose 18.7%, which shows the cost base can be held when revenue grows; and fifth, demonstrated access to the unsecured bond market in February 2026, with the notes valued at 97.50% of principal at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 49, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10–12, 24; calculation C04; calculation C09; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ranked weaknesses are, first, carrier buy rates that have risen faster than contract sell rates, taking cost of transportation from 75.6% to 82.5% of revenue and adjusted EBITDA margin to 1.77%; second, negative free cash flow of USD 73 million over the last twelve months that is funded by debt; third, reliance on add-backs that are 51.72% of adjusted EBITDA; fourth, overhead that absorbs 89.96% of gross profit, so small falls in gross profit cut earnings sharply; and fifth, event and documentation risk, because the sale terms for the debt and the covenant levels are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 10–11, 16, 21; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C08; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: RXO is a brokered transportation platform: it places shippers' freight with independent carriers and earns the spread between what the shipper pays and what the carrier is paid, so the company owns few assets and its cash flow depends on that spread more than on volume. Truck brokerage was 73.6% of 2025 revenue and 76.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue, last mile deliveries of heavy goods (where the issuer describes itself as the largest outsourced provider in the United States) were 20.8% and 18.6%, and managed transportation was 9.6% and 8.5%; about 8% of 2026 revenue arises outside the United States. Pricing is on a contract or spot basis, carriers are signed on non-exclusive one-year agreements and the firm fixed-consideration obligations the issuer counts beyond a year are only USD 51 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 18; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors this means weak cash-flow visibility, because revenue is short-dated and moves with freight rates, and a cost of transportation that moves with carrier rates, so the spread, not revenue, is what carries the debt. It supports liquidity preservation, because capital needs are small and discretionary, but it makes debt service depend on gross profit dollars and on management's ability to cut overhead, not on contracted income. Refinancing confidence rests on liquidity and the 2031 maturity profile rather than on revenue durability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 24; calculation C13; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: RXO is a listed company with no controlling holder: it was spun off from XPO in November 2022, had about 94 registered holders in February 2026 and one named holder of about 19%, MFN Partners LP, which has agreed to vote for the sale. It has never paid a cash dividend, funded the 2024 Coyote acquisition with about USD 1.1 billion of new equity rather than debt, and holds an unused repurchase authorization of USD 123 million, which points to a conservative leverage tolerance in the past. The notes are guaranteed by wholly owned domestic subsidiaries other than excluded subsidiaries, and the secured facility's credit agreement is between three named group companies, guarantors and lenders, with a first-priority security interest in the assets of the credit parties other than real property; the excluded subsidiaries and non-guarantor financials are not supplied, so structural priority cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 53, 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 15, 31–32; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit implication is that financial policy has been creditor-friendly, but the sale replaces it with the acquirer's policy, which the filings do not describe, and board independence cannot be judged because the proxy statement was not supplied. Creditor alignment under the standalone company is therefore reasonable on record and unproven on governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical, discretionary, rate-dependent and moderately concentrated, and it is regulated through carrier licensing but not structurally declining. In the third quarter of 2026 revenue rose by USD 450 million, of which truck brokerage supplied USD 394 million, mainly through a 48% rise in revenue per load driven by freight rates and fuel prices, while load volume rose 2%; in the nine months revenue per load rose 34% and the issuer's text on volume contradicts itself. Fuel passes through to revenue over time without a matching rise in gross profit, so higher revenue overstates real growth: gross profit rose 17.25% in the third quarter and 2.77% in the nine months against revenue growth of 31.7% and 18.7%. The consequence for credit is that revenue and receivables swell when rates rise and debt service must be judged on gross profit dollars, not on revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 21, 23; calculation C07; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is limited in both directions: contract sell rates lag carrier buy rates in a tight market, shippers soliciting bids from several providers can depress freight rates, and the pricing environment becomes more competitive in downturns. Customer concentration is moderate (largest customer 11.4%, top five 23%), retail and e-commerce are 37.4% of revenue, and the logistics and transportation vertical fell to USD 78 million in the third quarter from USD 123 million; the filings give no renewal or churn data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Most cost is variable: cost of transportation was 82.47% of nine-month 2026 revenue, so margin is set by the gap between what carriers charge and what customers pay, and the issuer states that capacity leaving the market after regulatory changes and enforcement made buy rates rise faster than contract sell rates in 2025 and 2026, while in 2024 the squeeze came from the other side, when lower freight rates were not fully offset by cheaper purchased transportation. Overhead is 15.62% of nine-month revenue and includes variable compensation, which rose in the third quarter with profit, and restructuring savings with operating leverage took SG&A to 11.9% of third-quarter revenue from 14.6%. Margins cannot be defended against a carrier-rate shock by pricing, as the three-year decline shows, and the defence so far has been overhead reduction, which is finite; against volume pressure the defence is better because carrier cost and variable pay fall with volume, but overhead of USD 1,039 million over the last twelve months does not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 49–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 21–23; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit implication is operating leverage on gross profit: overhead absorbs 89.96% of gross profit, and a 1 pp rise in cost of transportation removes USD 65.39 million, or 56.37% of adjusted EBITDA of USD 116 million. Fuel is a pass-through over time and fuel surcharges may not fully capture increases, and no wage inflation or input-cost data beyond that is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C10; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is low and flexible: USD 58 million over the last twelve months is 0.89% of revenue and 50.00% of adjusted EBITDA, and the issuer says it has significant discretion over amount and timing and is bound by no schedule. Cash interest was USD 29 million and cash taxes USD 7 million over the last twelve months, so adjusted EBITDA of USD 116 million leaves only USD 22 million before working capital and restructuring cash, and the issuer paid USD 25 million of restructuring cash in nine months with a USD 25 million reserve still open; operating lease liabilities of USD 231 million sit outside debt. Free cash flow was negative USD 73 million over the last twelve months, which is minus 62.93% of adjusted EBITDA, and negative in 2024 and 2025 as well.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 9, 24; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C15; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA does not currently translate into free cash flow available for debt service, deleveraging or liquidity preservation: the shortfall is covered by borrowing, mainly on the secured facility, and capital spending flexibility is the main lever over the 2031 wall. Volumes are typically higher in the fourth quarter, so the year-end working-capital pattern cannot be read from nine-month figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 25; calculation C05; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and sets the ceiling on pricing: the industry is fragmented with thousands of competitors, some with larger customer bases and more resources, and shippers solicit bids from several brokers, which presses rates and margins in weak markets and keeps contract sell rates from rising as fast as buy rates in tight ones. Threat of new entrants is not assessed in the filings beyond the fragmentation of the industry and management's claim of a technology advantage, which is not visible in margins that have fallen for three years. Substitutes matter through shippers building internal transportation capability, which the issuer names as a driver of results. Buyer power is moderate because the largest customer is 11.4% and the top five 23% of revenue, and the filings give no renewal terms. Carrier power is the force that shows in the numbers: one-year non-exclusive agreements and capacity exits raised buy rates faster than sell rates, and each 1 pp of revenue that shifts to carriers is worth USD 65.39 million of gross profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 11, 21, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C08; calculation C14; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Only the regulatory and economic factors materially alter the credit. Regulatory change and enforcement pushed capacity out of the truck market and lifted buy rates, which moved cost of transportation to 82.5% of revenue, and misclassification claims against last mile contractors are an unquantified tail risk; economic conditions drive volume, fuel and freight rates, and the issuer notes that recessions depress activity and that inflation hurts unless pricing follows. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are liquidity of USD 360 million, no large maturity before 2031, low capital intensity at 0.89% of revenue, moderate customer concentration and a cost base that has been cut. Weaknesses are an adjusted EBITDA margin of 1.77%, negative free cash flow, add-backs of 51.72% of adjusted EBITDA, tangible equity of negative USD 17 million and unknown covenant levels. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are contract sell rates catching up with carrier buy rates, which would widen the spread (an analyst inference; the 2024 report shows the spread narrowing when freight rates fell), continued overhead restraint, and a sale that places the debt under a stronger owner or repays it. Threats that could weaken it are further capacity exits that raise buy rates, a freight recession that cuts gross profit against fixed overhead, a failed or conditioned sale with a USD 175 million fee, and contractor misclassification claims.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 22, 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8, 10–12, 16, 21, 31; calculation C04; calculation C15; calculation C19; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are liquidity of USD 360 million, a debt stack with no large maturity before 2031, interest covered 4.00x by adjusted EBITDA, low capital intensity, moderate customer concentration and an overhead base that management has shown it can cut. The main constraints are a gross margin that has fallen from 24.45% to 17.53%, reported EBITDA of only USD 56 million over the last twelve months against debt of USD 496 million, free cash flow negative in each period, and reliance on add-backs that are 51.72% of adjusted EBITDA. The trend is mixed: leverage on adjusted EBITDA rose from 2.75x at the end of 2024 to 4.06x while third-quarter earnings improved, and the stated liquidity fell from USD 582 million at the end of 2025 to USD 360 million, although the old revolver's covenants limited usable capacity to USD 202 million, so usable liquidity then was nearer USD 219 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 52, 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10, 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The key missing datapoints are the covenant levels and borrowing base of the secured facility, a consolidated adjusted EBITDA stated by the issuer, the treatment of the debt in the merger, board and ownership detail from the proxy statement, and any contract or margin-per-load data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the issuer's own text says the market remained tight in the third quarter with capacity still exiting, so, as analyst judgement, cost of transportation is more likely to stay high than to fall and revenue will stay inflated by rates; the offset is continued overhead restraint, since transaction and integration costs fell to USD 7 million from USD 18 million in the nine months and restructuring reserves are being used. Cash interest on the 2031 notes is scheduled to start on 2026-11-15 (payment is not confirmed by the supplied filings), and run-rate cash interest of about USD 28.9 million is close to the USD 29 million paid over the last twelve months. A sale closing in the first half of 2027 would end the standalone period, so the outlook for creditors beyond that date depends on terms not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10–11, 21, 23; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the debt matures in 2031, the notes become callable from 2028-05-15 and the main sector tailwinds named by the issuer (broker penetration, digital adoption and e-commerce demand) are management statements that the margin history does not yet support, while the main headwinds are carrier pricing power, cyclical freight demand and legal change on contractor status.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a continuation of the pattern the issuer already reports, not a generic recession: capacity keeps leaving the market, carrier buy rates rise faster than contract sell rates, and cost of transportation rises a further 1 pp of revenue to 83.5% from 82.5%, a smaller step than the 2.2 pp rise between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026. The first operational break is gross profit, which falls by USD 65.39 million on last-twelve-month revenue while overhead of USD 1,039 million does not move quickly; adjusted EBITDA falls to USD 50.61 million, net debt over adjusted EBITDA rises to 9.31x from 4.06x and adjusted cover on cash interest falls to 1.75x. Free cash flow worsens from negative USD 73 million to about negative USD 138.39 million before any working-capital release, which USD 360 million of liquidity would cover for about 2.60 years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 21–23; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The observable triggers are cost of transportation above 82.5% of revenue with gross profit falling, a rise in borrowings on the secured facility, and any covenant waiver; the sale adds a second path, in which the deal fails or is conditioned, a USD 175 million fee is paid and customers and carriers drift during the wait. Management levers are variable compensation and further overhead reduction, capital spending that is discretionary, leaving the buyback authorization unused, repricing contracts as they renew (although the issuer says pricing turns more competitive in downturns), and a working-capital release if receivables shrink faster than payables. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over the next twelve months on stated availability, but not demonstrated against the fixed charge coverage and minimum availability tests whose levels are not stated, and this scenario is an analyst sensitivity, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rxo.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 16, 21, 24, 29–32; calculation C20; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, RXO presents an adequate business profile supported by an asset-light model, moderate customer concentration and USD 6,539 million of revenue, but credit quality is constrained by an adjusted EBITDA margin of 1.77%, add-backs of 51.72% of adjusted EBITDA and negative free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears weak because carrier buy rates have outrun sell rates for three years and earnings have been held up by operating leverage and overhead restraint, not margin. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on liquidity of USD 360 million, the 2031 maturity profile and the merger terms for the debt. The primary downside path is a further rise in cost of transportation against fixed overhead, with the sale leaving the debt terms open. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and note indenture, the merger agreement, the proxy statement and contract and margin-per-load data. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: carrier buy rates rising faster than sell rates while overhead absorbs most gross profit.
